newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 3.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The budget deficit for the first half decreased the first day of June by one-third to 10.5 billion crowns. This is primarily due a flood of revenues from taxes.

- Public insurer Vseobecna Zdravotni Pojistovna yesterday terminated its contract with Budejovicky policlinic, one of the largest Czech clinics, because doctors were collecting payments from patients. The insurance company's administrative council will meet today to discuss possibilities for paying doctors.

- Radio Alfa is threatened with losing its broadcasting licence for not fulfilling long-term conditions. The Council for Radio and Television Broadcasting this week began legal proceedings to revoke its licence.
- During 1996, the Czech Republic's gross debt amounted to $20.4 billion, of which debts for businesses were $9.7 billion and for commercial banks, $8.9 billion.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - Smokers who buy cigarettes made at Tabak will have to pay one crown more for King Size and 50 hellers more for 70 mm packages.
- State-owned Benzina, which currently controls about five percent of the Czech fuel market, will be privatised in a public tender, according to a cabinet decision yesterday.
- Ceska Rafinerska had net profits last year of nearly 866 million crowns. It was decided in a general meeting yesterday that no dividend will be paid.

- IPB bank recently sold some of its stakes in various companies. It sold 28.88 percent of Chlumcanske Keramicke Zavody, 10.17 percent of Obchodni Sladoven Prostejov and more than 16 percent of Plzensky Prazdroj to the Quartermaine Investment Fund B.V.
- For the first time in two weeks, the central bank placed funds on the money market at 18.25 percent.

- From today, Komercni Banka is decreasing its reference rate, base rate, and, with the exception of seven-day deposits with high balances, it is increasing rates on deposits with fixed interest rates and also its rates for all savings accounts with a termination deadline over one month.

- The Czech Statistical Bureau predicts that, by the end of this year, unemployment will increase to 4.8 percent, and next year it should be around five or six percent. This is due to the cabinet's latest measures and that many companies, including SPT Telecom and Czech Railways, are planning lay offs.
LIDOVE NOVINY - At the beginning of July, the Prague Stock Exchange began operating its own server on the Internet.

- Total revenue for insurance companies for the first quarter of this year amounted to 21.4 billion crowns an 18.7 percent increase over the same time last year. Total expenses were 22.2 billion crowns, a 13.7 percent year-on-year rise.

- By establishing the first division Skoda Energo on June 29, Skoda Plzen began its planned transition to division organisation according to field. Skoda Energo is made up of Skoda Turbiny, Skoda ETD, Skoda Elektricke Stroje, Skoda Controls and Skoda Diz.
- So far this year, the Budvar brewery has brewed 1,600 hectolitres of 17 degree Bud beer, which, with alcohol content of 7.2 percent, is the strongest Czech regular beer.

- During the second parliament reading yesterday, the opposition did not succeed in returning a series of new tax laws, including one to increase taxes on energy. If these are approved next week, consumer taxes on fuel, alcohol and cigarettes will increase, and taxes for businesses will decrease.
PRAVO - According to CSOB bank, the transactions mentioned for beginning forced administration of O.B. Invest are unauthorised.
